Count Proportions Out of the Full Sample

Source: R/full_sample.R
ck_full_sample_base.Rd

By default a respondent with no answer to a question - typically because skip logic never asked it - is outside the denominator of that question, so a question asked of 600 of 1,000 respondents reports n_total = 600. This puts those respondents back in the base:

Usage

ck_full_sample_base(
  dataset,
  loa,
  group_variables = NULL,
  label = "Not asked / no response",
  sm_separator = "/",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

dataset

The analysis dataset.

loa

The list of analyses, used to find the variables to act on.

group_variables

Grouping variables; these are never filled.

label

Row label for respondents with no answer, in select_one and select_multiple questions. Default "Not asked / no response".

sm_separator

Separator between parent and choice. Default "/".

verbose

Logical. Default TRUE.

Value

A list with dataset, filled (one row per variable: analysis_var, analysis_type, n_filled) and filled_vars (the variables that were filled).

Details

select_one

A blank answer becomes label (by default Not asked / no response), so it is reported as its own row and the question's rows add up to the whole sample.

select_multiple

A blank child (the question was not asked) becomes 0 (not selected), so every choice is a share of the full sample. A child column named label is added, 1 for respondents never asked and 0 for everyone else, so the not-asked share is its own row, last, in every column. The parent is filled with label too, because the survey engine reads who was asked from the parent.

Means, medians and ratios are left alone: a blank number cannot be averaged without inventing a value for it.

Run it after ck_sm_children_to_binary and before ck_exclude_choices, so that a choice excluded on purpose still leaves the denominator. A variable that is also a grouping variable is skipped, so the "Missing" group of a disaggregation is not renamed.
